podcast.body: Recorded in Los Angeles at Capitol Studios, the same studio famously used for The Beach Boys' "Pet Sounds." The recording process, which followed a two-month tour of America, was described as "madness" and "great." It was marked by an incident on the very first day when Bez was involved in a car crash and police chase on the highway near the studio. "Yeah, we did that in LA and we was away from it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1990, this album was a massive sensation both at home in the UK and internationally, contributing to Factory Records' high-flying status. It is characterized as the "everything" album, representing a period of extreme excess, whatever the band could get their hands on in LA. "Pills and Fruits was everything, was the LA, everything, whatever you can get all of in LA album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, released in 1990, marked a period of massive success for the band, both at home in England and internationally. The band considered this their "LA album," describing it as encompassing "everything, whatever you can get." The album's commercial performance contributed to Factory Records flying high. "The Happy Mondays in Loose Fits from the 1990 album Pills and Thrills and Belly Eggs."
